methods.name: bank
methods.description: Select the sound bank to use. To be used together with `s`. The bank name (+ "_") will be prepended to the value of `s`.

methods.name: begin
methods.description: A pattern of numbers from 0 to 1. Skips the beginning of each sample, e.g. `0.25` to cut off the first quarter from each sample.

params.name: amount
params.description: between 0 and 1, where 1 is the length of the sample

methods.name: byteBeatExpression
methods.description: Create byte beats with custom expressions

methods.name: byteBeatStartTime
methods.description: Create byte beats with custom expressions

methods.name: clip
methods.description: Multiplies the duration with the given number. Also cuts samples off at the end if they exceed the duration.

methods.name: cut
methods.description: In the style of classic drum-machines, `cut` will stop a playing sample as soon as another samples with in same cutgroup is to be played. An example would be an open hi-hat followed by a closed one, essentially muting the open.

methods.name: density
methods.description: Noise crackle density

methods.name: duration
methods.description: Sets the duration of the event in cycles. Similar to clip / legato, it also cuts samples off at the end if they exceed the duration.

methods.name: end
methods.description: The same as .begin, but cuts off the end off each sample.

params.name: length
params.description: 1 = whole sample, .5 = half sample, .25 = quarter sample etc..

methods.name: fit
methods.description: Makes the sample fit its event duration. Good for rhythmical loops like drum breaks. Similar to `loopAt`.

methods.name: loop
methods.description: Loops the sample. Note that the tempo of the loop is not synced with the cycle tempo. To change the loop region, use loopBegin / loopEnd.

methods.name: loopAt
methods.description: Makes the sample fit the given number of cycles by changing the speed.

methods.name: loopAtCps
methods.description: Makes the sample fit the given number of cycles and cps value, by changing the speed. Please note that at some point cps will be given by a global clock and this function will be deprecated/removed.

methods.name: loopBegin
methods.description: Begin to loop at a specific point in the sample (inbetween `begin` and `end`). Note that the loop point must be inbetween `begin` and `end`, and before `loopEnd`! Note: Samples starting with wt_ will automatically loop! (wt = wavetable)

params.name: time
params.description: between 0 and 1, where 1 is the length of the sample

methods.name: loopEnd
methods.description: End the looping section at a specific point in the sample (inbetween `begin` and `end`). Note that the loop point must be inbetween `begin` and `end`, and after `loopBegin`!

params.name: time
params.description: between 0 and 1, where 1 is the length of the sample

methods.name: n
methods.description: Selects the given index from the sample map. Numbers too high will wrap around. `n` can also be used to play midi numbers, but it is recommended to use `note` instead.

methods.name: noise
methods.description: Adds pink noise to the mix

methods.name: note
methods.description: Plays the given note name or midi number. A note name consists of

methods.name: partials
methods.description: Scale the magnitude of the harmonics of one of the core synths ('sine', 'tri', 'saw', ..)

params.name: magnitudes
params.description: List of [0, 1] magnitudes for partials. 0th entry is the fundamental harmonic (i.e. DC offset is skipped)

methods.name: phases
methods.description: Rotates the harmonics of one of the core synths ('sine', 'tri', 'saw', 'user', ..) by a list of phases

params.name: phases
params.description: List of [0, 1) phases for partials. 0th entry is the fundamental phase (i.e. DC offset is skipped)

methods.name: pw
methods.description: Controls the pulsewidth of the pulse oscillator

methods.name: pwrate
methods.description: Controls the lfo rate for the pulsewidth of the pulse oscillator

methods.name: pwsweep
methods.description: Controls the lfo sweep for the pulsewidth of the pulse oscillator

methods.name: s
methods.description: Select a sound / sample by name. When using mininotation, you can also optionally supply 'n' and 'gain' parameters separated by ':'.

params.name: sound
params.description: The sound / pattern of sounds to pick

methods.name: scrub
methods.description: Allows you to scrub an audio file like a tape loop by passing values that represents the position in the audio file in the optional array syntax ex: "0.5:2", the second value controls the speed of playback

methods.name: slice
methods.description: Chops samples into the given number of slices, triggering those slices with a given pattern of slice numbers. Instead of a number, it also accepts a list of numbers from 0 to 1 to slice at specific points.

methods.name: speed
methods.description: Changes the speed of sample playback, i.e. a cheap way of changing pitch.

params.name: speed
params.description: -inf to inf, negative numbers play the sample backwards.

methods.name: splice
methods.description: Works the same as slice, but changes the playback speed of each slice to match the duration of its step.

methods.name: stretch
methods.description: Changes the speed of sample playback, i.e. a cheap way of changing pitch.

params.name: factor
params.description: -inf to inf, negative numbers play the sample backwards.

methods.name: unison
methods.description: Set number of stacked voices for supported oscillators

methods.name: add
methods.description: Assumes a pattern of numbers. Adds the given number to each item in the pattern.

methods.name: arp
methods.description: Selects indices in in stacked notes.

methods.name: arpWith
methods.description: Selects indices in in stacked notes.

methods.name: detune
methods.description: Set detune for stacked voices of supported oscillators

methods.name: freq
methods.description: Set frequency of sound.

params.name: frequency
params.description: in Hz. the audible range is between 20 and 20000 Hz

methods.name: octave
methods.description: Sets the default octave of a synth.

methods.name: panchor
methods.description: Sets the range anchor of the envelope: - anchor 0: range = [note, note + penv] - anchor 1: range = [note - penv, note] If you don't set an anchor, the value will default to the psustain value.

methods.name: pattack
methods.description: Attack time of pitch envelope.

methods.name: pcurve
methods.description: Curve of envelope. Defaults to linear. exponential is good for kicks

methods.name: pdecay
methods.description: Decay time of pitch envelope.

methods.name: penv
methods.description: Amount of pitch envelope. Negative values will flip the envelope. If you don't set other pitch envelope controls, `pattack:.2` will be the default.

methods.name: prelease
methods.description: Release time of pitch envelope

methods.name: rootNotes
methods.description: Maps the chords of the incoming pattern to root notes in the given octave.

methods.name: scale
methods.description: Turns numbers into notes in the scale (zero indexed) or quantizes notes to a scale.
methods.note: needs note(); silent on a drum deck

methods.name: scaleTranspose
methods.description: Transposes notes inside the scale by the number of steps. Expected to be called on a Pattern which already has a scale

params.name: offset
params.description: number of steps inside the scale

methods.name: sub
methods.description: Like add, but the given numbers are subtracted.

methods.name: transpose
methods.description: Change the pitch of each value by the given amount. Expects numbers or note strings as values. The amount can be given as a number of semitones or as a string in interval short notation. If you don't care about enharmonic correctness, just use numbers. Otherwise, pass the interval of the form: ST where S is the degree number and T the type of interval with

params.name: amount
params.description: Either number of semitones or interval string.

methods.note: needs note(); silent on a drum deck

methods.name: vowel

params.name: vowel
params.description: You can use a e i o u ae aa oe ue y uh un en an on, corresponding to [a] [e] [i] [o] [u] [æ] [ɑ] [ø] [y] [ɯ] [ʌ] [œ̃] [ɛ̃] [ɑ̃] [ɔ̃]. Aliases: aa = å = ɑ, oe = ø = ö, y = ı, ae = æ.

methods.name: adsr
methods.description: ADSR envelope: Combination of Attack, Decay, Sustain, and Release.

methods.name: attack
methods.description: Amplitude envelope attack time: Specifies how long it takes for the sound to reach its peak value, relative to the onset.

methods.name: decay
methods.description: Amplitude envelope decay time: the time it takes after the attack time to reach the sustain level. Note that the decay is only audible if the sustain value is lower than 1.

methods.name: release
methods.description: Amplitude envelope release time: The time it takes after the offset to go from sustain level to zero.

methods.name: sustain
methods.description: Amplitude envelope sustain level: The level which is reached after attack / decay, being sustained until the offset.

methods.name: compressor
methods.description: Dynamics Compressor. The params are `compressor("threshold:ratio:knee:attack:release")` More info here

methods.name: gain
methods.description: Controls the gain by an exponential amount.

methods.name: postgain
methods.description: Gain applied after all effects have been processed.

methods.name: transient
methods.description: Transient shaper. Gives independent control over the emphasis on transients and sustains

params.name: sustain
params.description: Emphasis on the sustains; between -1 (deaccentuate) and 1 (accentuate)

methods.name: velocity
methods.description: Sets the velocity from 0 to 1. Is multiplied together with gain.

methods.name: duckattack
methods.description: The time required for the ducked signal(s) to return to their normal volume.
methods.note: needs .duckorbit(); orbits here are decks: 1 = deck A, 2 = deck B

methods.name: duckdepth
methods.description: The amount of ducking applied to target orbit
methods.note: needs .duckorbit(); orbits here are decks: 1 = deck A, 2 = deck B

methods.name: duckonset
methods.description: The time required for the ducked signal(s) to reach their lowest volume. Can be used to prevent clicking or for creative rhythmic effects.
methods.note: needs .duckorbit(); orbits here are decks: 1 = deck A, 2 = deck B

methods.name: duckorbit
methods.description: Modulate the amplitude of an orbit to create a "sidechain" like effect.
methods.note: orbits here are decks: 1 = deck A, 2 = deck B

methods.name: delay
methods.description: Sets the level of the delay signal.

methods.name: delayfeedback
methods.description: Sets the level of the signal that is fed back into the delay. Caution: Values >= 1 will result in a signal that gets louder and louder! Don't do it

methods.name: delayspeed
methods.description: Sets the time of the delay effect.

params.name: delayspeed
params.description: controls the pitch of the delay feedback

methods.name: delaysync
methods.description: Sets the time of the delay effect in cycles.

methods.name: irbegin
methods.description: Sets the beginning of the IR response sample

methods.name: iresponse

params.name: sample

methods.name: irspeed
methods.description: Sets speed of the sample for the impulse response.

methods.name: room
methods.description: Sets the level of reverb.

methods.name: roomdim

methods.name: roomfade
methods.description: Reverb fade time (in seconds). When this property is changed, the reverb will be recaculated, so only change this sparsely..

methods.name: roomlp
methods.description: Reverb lowpass starting frequency (in hertz). When this property is changed, the reverb will be recaculated, so only change this sparsely..

methods.name: roomsize

methods.name: chorus
methods.description: mix control for the chorus effect

methods.name: env
methods.description: Configures an envelope. Can be called in sequence like pat.env(...).env(...) to set up multiple envelopes There are two ways to declare which control will be modulated: 1. Explicitly put `control` in the config (e.g. `env({ c: "lpf" })`) 2. If the control parameter is absent, the control _immediately before_ the `env` call will be used (e.g. `s("saw").lpf(500).env({ a: 1 })` to modulate `lpf`)

params.name: [config.subControl]

params.name: [config.dcurve]

params.name: [config.rcurve]

methods.name: fmattack
methods.description: Attack time for the FM envelope: time it takes to reach maximum modulation

methods.name: fmdecay

methods.name: fmenv
methods.description: Ramp type of fm envelope. Exp might be a bit broken..

methods.name: fmh
methods.description: Sets the Frequency Modulation Harmonicity Ratio. Controls the timbre of the sound. Whole numbers and simple ratios sound more natural, while decimal numbers and complex ratios sound metallic.

methods.name: fmi
methods.description: Sets the Frequency Modulation of the synth. Controls the modulation index, which defines the brightness of the sound.

methods.name: fmrelease
methods.description: Release time for the FM envelope: how much modulation is applied after the note is released

methods.name: fmsustain
methods.description: Sustain level for the FM envelope: how much modulation is applied after the decay phase

methods.name: fmwave
methods.description: Waveform of the fm modulator

methods.name: lfo

If the control parameter is absent, the control _immediately before_ the `lfo` call will be used (e.g. `s("saw").lpf(500).lfo()` to modulate `lpf`)

params.name: [config.subControl]

params.name: id
params.description: ID to use for this modulator

methods.name: phaserdepth

methods.name: distorttype

methods.name: distortvol

methods.name: drive

methods.name: fold

methods.name: hard

methods.name: sinefold

methods.name: soft

methods.name: jux
methods.description: The jux function creates strange stereo effects, by applying a function to a pattern, but only in the right-hand channel.

methods.name: juxBy
methods.description: Jux with adjustable stereo width. 0 = mono, 1 = full stereo.

methods.name: pan
methods.description: Sets position in stereo.

params.name: pan
params.description: between 0 and 1, from left to right (assuming stereo), once round a circle (assuming multichannel)

methods.name: spread
methods.description: Set the stereo pan spread for supported oscillators

methods.name: bite
methods.description: Splits a pattern into the given number of slices, and plays them according to a pattern of slice numbers. Similar to `slice`, but slices up patterns rather than sound samples.

methods.name: brak
methods.description: Returns a new pattern where every other cycle is played once, twice as fast, and offset in time by one quarter of a cycle. Creates a kind of breakbeat feel.

methods.name: chop
methods.description: Cuts each sample into the given number of parts, allowing you to explore a technique known as 'granular synthesis'. It turns a pattern of samples into a pattern of parts of samples.

methods.name: compress
methods.description: Compress each cycle into the given timespan, leaving a gap

methods.name: early
methods.description: Nudge a pattern to start earlier in time. Equivalent of Tidal's <~ operator

params.name: cycles
params.description: number of cycles to nudge left

methods.name: echo
methods.description: Superimpose and offset multiple times, gradually decreasing the velocity

methods.name: echoWith
methods.description: Superimpose and offset multiple times, applying the given function each time.

params.name: func
params.description: function to apply, given the pattern and the iteration index

methods.name: fast
methods.description: Speed up a pattern by the given factor. Used by "*" in mini notation.

methods.name: fastGap
methods.description: speeds up a pattern like fast, but rather than it playing multiple times as fast would it instead leaves a gap in the remaining space of the cycle. For example, the following will play the sound pattern "bd sn" only once but compressed into the first half of the cycle, i.e. twice as fast.

methods.name: focus
methods.description: Similar to `compress`, but doesn't leave gaps, and the 'focus' can be bigger than a cycle

methods.name: hurry
methods.description: Both speeds up the pattern (like 'fast') and the sample playback (like 'speed').

methods.name: iter
methods.description: Divides a pattern into a given number of subdivisions, plays the subdivisions in order, but increments the starting subdivision each cycle. The pattern wraps to the first subdivision after the last subdivision is played.

methods.name: iterBack
methods.description: Like `iter`, but plays the subdivisions in reverse order. Known as iter' in tidalcycles

methods.name: late
methods.description: Nudge a pattern to start later in time. Equivalent of Tidal's ~> operator

params.name: cycles
params.description: number of cycles to nudge right

methods.name: linger
methods.description: Selects the given fraction of the pattern and repeats that part to fill the remainder of the cycle.

methods.name: off
methods.description: Superimposes the function result on top of the original pattern, delayed by the given time.

methods.name: palindrome
methods.description: Applies `rev` to a pattern every other cycle, so that the pattern alternates between forwards and backwards.

methods.name: ply
methods.description: The ply function repeats each event the given number of times.

methods.name: plyForEach
methods.description: The plyForEach function repeats each event the given number of times, applying the given function to each event. This version of ply uses the iteration index as an argument to the function, similar to echoWith.

params.name: func
params.description: function to apply, given the pattern and the iteration index

methods.name: plyWith
methods.description: The plyWith function repeats each event the given number of times, applying the given function to each event.

params.name: func
params.description: function to apply, given the pattern

methods.name: press
methods.description: Syncopates a rhythm, by shifting each event halfway into its timespan.

methods.name: pressBy
methods.description: Like press, but allows you to specify the amount by which each event is shifted. pressBy(0.5) is the same as press, while pressBy(1/3) shifts each event by a third of its timespan.

methods.name: repeatCycles
methods.description: Repeats each cycle the given number of times.

methods.name: rev
methods.description: Reverse all cycles in a pattern. See also `revv` for reversing a whole pattern.

methods.name: revv
methods.description: Reverse a whole pattern. See also `rev` for reversing each cycle.

methods.name: ribbon
methods.description: Loops the pattern inside an `offset` for `cycles`. If you think of the entire span of time in cycles as a ribbon, you can cut a single piece and loop it.

params.name: offset
params.description: start point of loop in cycles

methods.name: scramble
methods.description: Slices a pattern into the given number of parts, then plays those parts at random. Similar to `shuffle`, but parts might be played more than once, or not at all, per cycle.

methods.name: segment
methods.description: Samples the pattern at a rate of n events per cycle. Useful for turning a continuous pattern into a discrete one.

methods.name: shuffle
methods.description: Slices a pattern into the given number of parts, then plays those parts in random order. Each part will be played exactly once per cycle.

methods.name: slow
methods.description: Slow down a pattern over the given number of cycles. Like the "/" operator in mini notation.

methods.name: striate
methods.description: Cuts each sample into the given number of parts, triggering progressive portions of each sample at each loop.

methods.name: stut
methods.description: Deprecated. Like echo, but the last 2 parameters are flipped.

methods.name: swing
methods.description: Shorthand for swingBy with 1/3:

methods.name: swingBy
methods.description: The function `swingBy x n` breaks each cycle into `n` slices, and then delays events in the second half of each slice by the amount `x`, which is relative to the size of the (half) slice. So if `x` is 0 it does nothing, `0.5` delays for half the note duration, and 1 will wrap around to doing nothing again. The end result is a shuffle or swing-like rhythm

methods.name: zoom
methods.description: Plays a portion of a pattern, specified by the beginning and end of a time span. The new resulting pattern is played over the time period of the original pattern:

methods.name: almostAlways
methods.description: Shorthand for `.sometimesBy(0.9, fn)`

methods.name: almostNever
methods.description: Shorthand for `.sometimesBy(0.1, fn)`

methods.name: always
methods.description: Shorthand for `.sometimesBy(1, fn)` (always calls fn)

methods.name: beat
methods.description: creates a structure pattern from divisions of a cycle especially useful for creating rhythms

methods.name: chunk
methods.description: Divides a pattern into a given number of parts, then cycles through those parts in turn, applying the given function to each part in turn (one part per cycle).

methods.name: chunkBack
methods.description: Like `chunk`, but cycles through the parts in reverse order. Known as chunk' in tidalcycles

methods.name: chunkBackInto
methods.description: Like `chunkInto`, but moves backwards through the chunks.

methods.name: chunkInto
methods.description: Like `chunk`, but the function is applied to a looped subcycle of the source pattern.

methods.name: degrade
methods.description: Randomly removes 50% of events from the pattern. Shorthand for `.degradeBy(0.5)`

methods.name: degradeBy
methods.description: Randomly removes events from the pattern by a given amount. 0 = 0% chance of removal 1 = 100% chance of removal

methods.name: euclid
methods.description: Changes the structure of the pattern to form an Euclidean rhythm. Euclidean rhythms are rhythms obtained using the greatest common divisor of two numbers. They were described in 2004 by Godfried Toussaint, a Canadian computer scientist. Euclidean rhythms are really useful for computer/algorithmic music because they can describe a large number of rhythms with a couple of numbers.

params.name: steps
params.description: the number of steps to fill

methods.name: euclidLegato
methods.description: Similar to `euclid`, but each pulse is held until the next pulse, so there will be no gaps.

params.name: steps
params.description: the number of steps to fill

methods.name: euclidLegatoRot
methods.description: Similar to `euclid`, but each pulse is held until the next pulse, so there will be no gaps, and has an additional parameter for 'rotating' the resulting sequence

params.name: steps
params.description: the number of steps to fill

methods.name: euclidRot
methods.description: Like `euclid`, but has an additional parameter for 'rotating' the resulting sequence.

params.name: steps
params.description: the number of steps to fill

methods.name: euclidish
methods.description: A 'euclid' variant with an additional parameter that morphs the resulting rhythm from 0 (no morphing) to 1 (completely 'even'). For example `sound("bd").euclidish(3,8,0)` would be the same as `sound("bd").euclid(3,8)`, and `sound("bd").euclidish(3,8,1)` would be the same as `sound("bd bd bd")`. `sound("bd").euclidish(3,8,0.5)` would have a groove somewhere between. Inspired by the work of Malcom Braff.

params.name: steps
params.description: the number of steps to fill

params.name: groove
params.description: exists between the extremes of 0 (straight euclidian) and 1 (straight pulse)

methods.name: every
methods.description: An alias for `firstOf`

methods.name: fastChunk
methods.description: Like `chunk`, but the cycles of the source pattern aren't repeated for each set of chunks.

methods.name: filter
methods.description: Filters haps using the given function

methods.name: filterWhen
methods.description: Filters haps by their begin time

methods.name: firstOf
methods.description: Applies the given function every n cycles, starting from the first cycle.

methods.name: inside
methods.description: Carries out an operation 'inside' a cycle.

methods.name: lastOf
methods.description: Applies the given function every n cycles, starting from the last cycle.

methods.name: mask
methods.description: Returns silence when mask is 0 or "~"

methods.name: never
methods.description: Shorthand for `.sometimesBy(0, fn)` (never calls fn)

methods.name: often
methods.description: Shorthand for `.sometimesBy(0.75, fn)`

methods.name: outside
methods.description: Carries out an operation 'outside' a cycle.

methods.name: rarely
methods.description: Shorthand for `.sometimesBy(0.25, fn)`

methods.name: reset
methods.description: Resets the pattern to the start of the cycle for each onset of the reset pattern.

methods.name: restart
methods.description: Restarts the pattern for each onset of the restart pattern. While reset will only reset the current cycle, restart will start from cycle 0.

methods.name: seed
methods.description: Change the seed for random signals. Normally, random signals depend on time, so two patterns at the same time will have the same random values. Specifying a new seed changes the signal output by `rand`. This also affects other functions that use randomness, like `shuffle` and `sometimes`.

params.name: n
params.description: A new seed. Can be any number.

methods.name: someCycles
methods.description: Shorthand for `.someCyclesBy(0.5, fn)`

methods.name: someCyclesBy
methods.description: Randomly applies the given function by the given probability on a cycle by cycle basis. Similar to `sometimesBy`

methods.name: sometimes
methods.description: Applies the given function with a 50% chance

methods.name: sometimesBy
methods.description: Randomly applies the given function by the given probability. Similar to `someCyclesBy`

methods.name: struct
methods.description: Applies the given structure to the pattern:

methods.name: undegrade
methods.description: Inverse of `degrade`: Randomly removes 50% of events from the pattern. Shorthand for `.undegradeBy(0.5)` Events that would be removed by degrade are let through by undegrade and vice versa (see second example).

methods.name: undegradeBy
methods.description: Inverse of `degradeBy`: Randomly removes events from the pattern by a given amount. 0 = 100% chance of removal 1 = 0% chance of removal Events that would be removed by degradeBy are let through by undegradeBy and vice versa (see second example).

methods.name: when
methods.description: Applies the given function whenever the given pattern is in a true state.

methods.name: within
methods.description: Use within to apply a function to only a part of a pattern.

params.name: end
params.description: end within cycle (0 - 1). Must be > start

params.name: func
params.description: function to be applied to the sub-pattern

methods.name: FX
methods.description: Establishes an FX chain. Can be called by chaining .FX(fx1).FX(fx2).. calls and/or in a single .FX(fx1, fx2, ..) call. The fx1, .. are _patterns_ which establish the controls of the given effect. See examples.

methods.name: apply
methods.description: Like layer, but with a single function:

methods.name: as
methods.description: Sets properties in a batch.

params.name: mapping
params.description: the control names that are set

methods.note: needs a pattern of plain values, e.g. "c3:.5 e3:1"

methods.name: bmod
methods.description: Modulates with the output from a given `bus`. Can be called in sequence like pat.bmod(...).bmod(...) to set up multiple modulators

params.name: [config.bus]
params.description: Bus to get modulation signal from

params.name: [config.subControl]
params.description: Sub-control name to append to the control key. Aliases: sc

params.name: [config.depth]
params.description: Relative modulation depth. Aliases: dep, dr

params.name: id
params.description: ID to use for this modulator

methods.note: needs a pattern sending to that bus with .bus()

methods.name: bus
methods.description: A `bus` is a send which can be used for mixing patterns. It combines with.. s("bus") to play that bus through another pattern (for, say, applying non-linear effects like distortion to multiple signals)
methods.note: heard through a pattern that plays s("bus")

methods.name: busgain
methods.description: Postgain multiplier prior to sending the signal to the audio bus.

methods.name: contract
methods.description: Experimental: Contracts the step size of the pattern by the given factor. See also `expand`.

methods.name: div
methods.description: Divides each number by the given factor.

methods.name: drop
methods.description: Experimental: Drops the given number of steps from a pattern. A positive number will drop steps from the start of a pattern, and a negative number from the end.

methods.name: expand
methods.description: Experimental: Expands the step size of the pattern by the given factor.

methods.name: extend
methods.description: Experimental: `extend` is similar to `fast` in that it increases its density, but it also increases the step count accordingly. So `stepcat("a b".extend(2), "c d")` would be the same as `"a b a b c d"`, whereas `stepcat("a b".fast(2), "c d")` would be the same as `"[a b] [a b] c d"`.

methods.name: grow
methods.description: Experimental: Progressively grows the pattern by 'n' steps until the full pattern is played, or if a second value is given (using mininotation list syntax with `:`), that number of times. A positive number will progressively grow steps from the start of a pattern, and a negative number from the end.

methods.name: into
methods.description: Breaks a pattern into pieces according to the structure of a given pattern. True values in the given pattern cause the corresponding subcycle of the source pattern to be looped, and for an (optional) given function to be applied. False values result in the corresponding part of the source pattern to be played unchanged.

methods.name: layer
methods.description: Layers the result of the given function(s). Like `superimpose`, but without the original pattern:

methods.name: mul
methods.description: Multiplies each number by the given factor.

methods.name: pace
methods.description: Experimental: Speeds a pattern up or down, to fit to the given number of steps per cycle.

methods.name: replicate
methods.description: Experimental: `replicate` is similar to `fast` in that it increases its density, but it also increases the step count accordingly. So `stepcat("a b".replicate(2), "c d")` would be the same as `"a b a b c d"`, whereas `stepcat("a b".fast(2), "c d")` would be the same as `"[a b] [a b] c d"`.

methods.name: shrink
methods.description: Experimental: Progressively shrinks the pattern by 'n' steps until there's nothing left, or if a second value is given (using mininotation list syntax with `:`), that number of times. A positive number will progressively drop steps from the start of a pattern, and a negative number from the end.

methods.name: superimpose
methods.description: Superimposes the result of the given function(s) on top of the original pattern:

methods.name: take
methods.description: Experimental: Takes the given number of steps from a pattern (dropping the rest). A positive number will take steps from the start of a pattern, and a negative number from the end.

methods.name: tour
methods.description: Experimental: Inserts a pattern into a list of patterns. On the first repetition it will be inserted at the end of the list, then moved backwards through the list on successive repetitions. The patterns are added together stepwise, with all repetitions taking place over a single cycle. Using `pace` to set the number of steps per cycle is therefore usually recommended.

methods.name: xfade
methods.description: Cross-fades between left and right from 0 to 1: - 0 = (full left, no right) - .5 = (both equal) - 1 = (no left, full right)
